Commentary.Commentary: The stage is set for South Africa's chase as the openers take to the field. Lhuan-dre Pretorius and Reeza Hendricks walk out to bat, with Richard Ngarava set to bowl the first over. The crowd is on the edge of their seats as South Africa begins its pursuit of the target!
...THE RUN CHASE...

Chasing a target of 142, South Africa will back themselves to get over the line and register their first win in the tri-series. Can they do it, or will Zimbabwe bowlers spring a surprise? We shall find out. Join us shortly for the second essay.

Ryan Burl is up for a chat. He says that they played too many dots. Adds that the conversation with Raza was to find boundaries and get the gaps to take twos. Shares that the wicket is on the slower side and it's keeping lower, but thinks the total is a bit under par. Adds that they have defended lower targets but says that they need to take a leaf out of Nandre Burger and Lungi Ngidi on the way they bowled today.

For the Proteas, George Linde stood out with the ball, claiming three wickets, while Lungi Ngidi and Nandre Burger delivered economical spells and chipped in with a wicket each. However, Corbin Bosch and Andile Simelane were expensive, allowing Zimbabwe to build momentum in the latter stages of the innings.

South Africa have delivered a disciplined bowling performance to hold Zimbabwe to a modest total of 141/6 in their allotted 20 overs. After being put in to bat, Zimbabwe lost Wessly Madhevere early, and Clive Madande struggled to find any rhythm at the crease. Brian Bennett played a few attractive strokes but couldn’t convert his start into a significant score. At 55/3 in the 11th over, the hosts were under pressure when Sikandar Raza and Ryan Burl steadied the innings with a valuable 66-run partnership for the fourth wicket. Burl fell for 29, but Raza continued to anchor the innings, finishing unbeaten with a well-compiled fifty that helped Zimbabwe cross the 140-run mark.
A couple of runs to end the innings! Low full toss on the middle and leg. Sikandar Raza flicks it toward deep mid-wicket and takes two runs. Zimbabwe finish on 141/6.

Commentary.Commentary: Done with the pre-match formalities and all set for the action to commence. The pair of Wessly Madhevere and Brian Bennett will open the innings for Zimbabwe. It will be Lungi Ngidi with the ball for South Africa. Let's play...

All in readiness now. The teams and the match officials are making their way to the middle for the National Anthems. We start with the anthem of South Africa, followed by that of the home side, Zimbabwe. Live action is coming shortly.

Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Rubin Hermann, and Corbin Bosch will be making their T20Is debut for South Africa today. For Zimbabwe, no debutants, and they are going with three pacers and a couple of spinners.

Pitch Report - Shaun Pollock is at the pitchside. Says that it’s a beautiful day and the players will be comfortable. Mentions that the square boundaries are 78m and 70m, while the straight hit is 70m. Further adds that the groundsmen have taken the grass off, which is expected, and the wicket is nice and hard. Says that there may be some purchase for the spinners, and the pacers can bowl off-pace deliveries. Overall, he finds it an interesting surface for the T20s.

Sikandar Raza, the Zimbabwe skipper, says that an early start in winter would have been difficult, but says that the wicket looks okay and the ball goes a bit. Adds that they need to put their best foot forward and keep the Test matches behind. Shares that they have no debutants today and are going with three spinners and three seamers.

Rassie van der Dussen, the skipper of South Africa, wins the toss and opts to bowl first. Says that it looks rock hard and doesn't think it will change much. Hopes for the seamers to get some help. Adds that the Test guys are coming off a massive high, and they are coming up against two good teams. Shares that they need to focus on playing good cricket. Adds that they have two debutants. Closes by saying that Corbin Bosch has had a great 6-8 months, and he is happy to have Nandre Burger back.

South Africa (Playing XI) - Lhuan-dre Pretorius(WK), Reeza Hendricks, Rassie van der Dussen(C), Rubin Hermann, Dewald Brevis, George Linde, Corbin Bosch, Andile Simelane, Nqabayomzi Peter, Nandre Burger, Lungi Ngidi.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Brian Bennett, Wessly Madhevere, Clive Madande(WK), Sikandar Raza(C), Ryan Burl, Tony Munyonga, Tashinga Musekiwa, Wellington Masakadza, Richard Ngarava, Blessing Muzarabani, Trevor Gwandu.
Toss Update - South Africa have won the toss and opted to BOWL.

For South Africa, Rassie van der Dussen will lead the side that is missing several senior players, while Reeza Hendricks, Lungi Ngidi, and Corbin Bosch are the experienced players in the side. The likes of Lhuan-dre Pretorius, Dewald Brevis, Kwena Maphaka, and Gerald Coetzee have done well at the international stage in their limited opportunities and will be keen to impress and stay in the reckoning. Rubin Hermann, getting his first call-up, will be eager to show his calibre. Overall, South Africa have a strong side and will look to start the Tri-Series on a winning note. So, who are you backing to emerge victorious? We shall find out. Toss and team news coming up shortly. Stay tuned!

The home side has named a strong squad for the T20Is, with Sikandar Raza returning to lead the Chevrons. Brian Bennett, Dion Myers, and Ryan Burl have been performing well with the bat recently. Trevor Gwandu and Tashinga Musekiwa are the fresh faces on the side and will be the ones to keep an eye on for the future.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the T20I Tri-Series between Zimbabwe, South Africa, and New Zealand. The first game will be between the hosts, Zimbabwe and South Africa, at the Harare Sports Club in Harare. After disappointing results in the recently concluded Test series, Zimbabwe will look to bounce back in the shortest format, while the Proteas will look to test their bench strength ahead of next year’s T20 World Cup.

We have a Tri Series at our disposal after a long time and it will be a series between Zimbabwe, South Africa and New Zealand. The stage is set for an exciting encounter as Zimbabwe hosts South Africa in the 1st T20I match of the Tri Series at the Harare Sports Club. Sikandar Raza's Zimbabwe will aim to cause an upset against a potent South African side, led by Rassie van der Dussen, which has been in impressive form. With players like Reeza Hendricks, Dewald Brevis, and young sensation Lhuan-dre Pretorius likely to play key roles, South Africa looks formidable. The batting-friendly pitch and favorable weather conditions promise an entertaining match. While Zimbabwe will need to perform at their best to pull off a win, South Africa will look to build on their recent momentum and take a lead in the series. Can Zimbabwe pull off a surprise, or will South Africa's strong form continue? We shall see soon.
